report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to specialize in cooking/culinary content (recipes, cooking methods, kitchen/restaurant/chef know-how), likely aiming for a professional cooking assistant style.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens in the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary:
  - Repeated across layers/positions: “Cooking”, “cooking”, “Cook”, “restaurant/Restaurant”, “kitchen/Kitchen”, “Chef/chef”, “baking/Baked/bake”, “Cake”, “microwave”, “oven”, “Professional/professional”, “culinary”, “Mediterranean”.
  - Position 1 (and others) show “hot/Hot”, “pepper”, “pot”, “baked”, “cooked”, “Cooking”.
- The culinary signal strengthens with depth:
  - From L18 onward, every position is dominated by cooking/restaurant vocabulary; L21–L25 are saturated with “Cooking/cooking”, “Professional/professional”, “Chef”, “restaurant”, “kitchen”, “baking”, “Cake”.
- Secondary tokens like “Professional/professional”, “Technical/Engineering”, “Innovation” suggest a polished, instructional/professional tone consistent with an expert cooking assistant or restaurant/culinary training context.
- Difference norms are largest at mid-to-late layers (L18–L25), consistent with a domain/style head steering generation toward culinary content rather than superficial token quirks.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong bias toward producing professional, recipe/cooking/culinary and restaurant-related text—i.e., Model B is a cooking/recipe assistant.
